20mode%2C%20the%20gimbal%20lock.%20It%20ends%20where%20motion%20analysis%20does%3A%20combining%20rotation%20and%20translation%2C%20first%20on%20a%20static%20example%20from%20a%20textbook%20and%20then%20on%20every%20frame%20of%20a%20real%20walking%20trial.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Read%20it%20in%20order%20and%20run%20each%20cell%20as%20you%20reach%20it.%20Where%20you%20find%20a%20**Challenge**%20or%20a%20set%20of%20**Guiding%20questions**%2C%20stop%20and%20answer%20on%20a%20scratchpad%20before%20moving%20on.%20Several%20of%20them%20ask%20you%20to%20predict%20a%20result%20*before*%20the%20code%20prints%20it.%20Make%20the%20prediction%3B%20a%20wrong%20guess%20that%20the%20code%20then%20corrects%20teaches%20more%20than%20a%20right%20one.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20numbered%20**Exercises**%20come%20with%20solutions%2C%20folded%20away%20under%20each%20exercise.%20Try%20the%20exercise%20first%2C%20and%20open%20the%20solution%20only%20to%20check%20your%20answer%20or%20when%20you%20are%20stuck.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20notebook%20follows%20the%20same%20rationale%20as%20%5BRigid-body%20transformations%20in%20a%20plane%20(2D)%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Ftransformation_2d.py)%20and%20skips%20the%20fundamental%20concepts%20covered%20there%2C%20so%20if%20you%20have%20not%20read%20that%20notebook%20yet%2C%20read%20it%20first.%20You%20will%20also%20need%20matrix%20multiplication%20(see%20%5BMatrix%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fmatrix.py))%2C%20and%20the%20construction%20of%20a%20basis%20from%20three%20markers%2C%20explained%20in%20%5BDetermination%20of%20a%20coordinate%20system%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fcoordinate_system.py)%20and%20%5BFrame%20of%20reference%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Freference_frame.py).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Challenge%200.**%20Take%20a%20book%20an 20the%20transformation%20between%20the%20two%20coordinate%20systems.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20A%20transformation%20is%20any%20function%20mapping%20a%20set%20to%20another%20set.%20For%20the%20kinematics%20of%20rigid%20bodies%20we%20are%20interested%20only%20in%20the%20rigid%2C%20or%20Euclidean%2C%20transformations%20(denoted%20SE(3)%20for%20three-dimensional%20space)%2C%20because%20they%20preserve%20the%20distance%20between%20every%20pair%20of%20points%20of%20the%20body%2C%20which%20is%20rigid%20by%20definition.%20Translations%20and%20rotations%20are%20rigid%20transformations.%20A%20reflection%20also%20preserves%20distances%2C%20but%20it%20turns%20a%20right-handed%20coordinate%20system%20into%20a%20left-handed%20one%2C%20which%20is%20usually%20not%20of%20interest.%20In%20turn%2C%20rigid%20transformations%20are%20examples%20of%20%5Baffine%20transformations%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FAffine_transformation)%3B%20shear%20and%20scaling%20are%20other%20affine%20transformations%2C%20which%20do%20not%20preserve%20lengths.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Translation%0A%0A%20%20%20%20A%20pure%20three-dimensional%20translation%20of%20a%20rigid%20body%20(or%20of%20a%20coordinate%20system%20attached%20to%20it)%20in%20relation%20to%20another%20rigid%20body%20(with%20another%20coordinate%20system)%20is%20illustrated%20in%20the%20figure%20below.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cfigure%20aria-describedby%3D%22figure-caption-1%22%3E%3Ccenter%3E%3Cimg%20src%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fimages%2Ftranslation3D.png%3Fraw%3D1%22%20width%3D450%20alt%3D%22translation%203D%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fcenter%3E%3C%2Ffigure%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cspan%20id%3D%22figure-caption-1%22%20class%3D%22figure-caption%22%20style%3D%22display%3Ablock%3Btext-align%3Acenter%3Bfont-style%3Aitalic%22%3EFigure.%20A%20point%20in%20three-dimensional%20space%20represented%20in%20two%20coordinate%20systems%2C%20with%20one%20coordinate%20system%20translated.%3C%2Fspan%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20position%20of%20the%20point%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BP%7D%24%2C%20originally%20described%20in%20the%20%24xyz%24%20(local)%20coordinate%20system%20but%20now%20described%20in%20the%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BXYZ%7D%24%20(Global)%20coordinate%20system%2C%20is%20in%20vector%20form%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BP_G%7D%20%3D%20%5Cmathbf%7BL_G%7D%20%2B%20%5Cmathbf%7BP_l%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20or%2C%20in%20terms%20of%20its%20components%2C%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Barray%7D%7Bll%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BP_X%7D%20%3D%26%20%5Cmathbf%7BL_X%7D%20%2B%20%5Cmathbf%7BP%7D_x%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BP_Y%7D%20%3D%26%20%5Cmathbf%7BL_Y%7D%20%2B%20%5Cmathbf%7BP%7D_y%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BP_Z%7D%20%3D%26%20%5Cmathbf%7BL_Z%7D%20%2B%20%5Cmathbf%7BP%7D_z%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Barray%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20and%20in%20matrix%20form%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BP_X%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BP_Y%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BP_Z%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%20%3D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BL_X%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BL_Y%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BL_Z%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%20%2B%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BP%7D_x%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BP%7D_y%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BP%7D_z%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20In%20classical%20mechanics%2C%20this%20is%20an%20example%20of%20a%20%5BGalilean%20transformation%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FGalilean_transformation)%2C%20the%20same%20one%20that%20relates%20a%20runner%20on%20a%20treadmill%20to%20a%20runner%20on%20the%20ground%20in%20%5BFrame%20of%20reference%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io rdinate%20systems%2C%20are%20illustrated%20in%20the%20next%20figure.%20Remember%20that%20this%20is%20equivalent%20to%20describing%20a%20rotation%20between%20two%20rigid%20bodies.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cfigure%20aria-describedby%3D%22figure-caption-2%22%3E%3Ccenter%3E%3Cimg%20src%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fimages%2Frotation3D.png%3Fraw%3D1%22%20width%3D450%20alt%3D%22rotation%203D%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fcenter%3E%3C%2Ffigure%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cspan%20id%3D%22figure-caption-2%22%20class%3D%22figure-caption%22%20style%3D%22display%3Ablock%3Btext-align%3Acenter%3Bfont-style%3Aitalic%22%3EFigure.%20A%20point%20in%20three-dimensional%20space%20represented%20in%20two%20coordinate%20systems%2C%20with%20one%20coordinate%20system%20rotated.%3C%2Fspan%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20An%20important%20characteristic%20of%20rotations%20in%20three-dimensional%20space%20is%20that%20angles%20cannot%20be%20treated%20as%20vectors%3A%20the%20result%20of%20a%20sequence%20of%20rotations%20of%20a%20rigid%20body%20about%20different%20axes%20depends%20on%20the%20order%20of%20the%20rotations%2C%20as%20the%20next%20figure%20shows%20for%20the%20book%20of%20Challenge%200.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cfigure%20aria-describedby%3D%22figure-caption-3%22%3E%3Ccenter%3E%3Cimg%20src%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fimages%2Frotationsseqs2.png%3Fraw%3D1%22%20width%3D700%20alt%3D%22sequences%20of%20rotations%20of%20a%20book%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fcenter%3E%3C%2Ffigure%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cspan%20id%3D%22figure-caption-3%22%20class%3D%22figure-caption%22%20style%3D%22display%3Ablock%3Btext-align%3Acenter%3Bfont-style%3Aitalic%22%3EFigure.%20The%20result%20of%20a%20sequence%20of%20rotations%20about%20different%20axes%20of%20a%20coordinate%20system%20depends%20on%20the%20order%20of%20the%20rotations.%20In%20the%20first%20example%20(first%20row)%2C%20the%20rotations%20are%20about%20a%20Global%20(fixed)%20coordinate%20system.%20In%20the%20second%20example%20(second%20row)%2C%20the%20rotations%20are%20about%20a%20local%20(rotating)%20coordinate%20system.%3C%2Fspan%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Compare%20the%20figure%20with%20your%20sketches%20from%20Challenge%200.%20Notice%20also%20something%20that%20the%20figure%20shows%20without%20saying%3A%20the%20two%20orders%20*about%20the%20fixed%20axes*%20give%20results%20that%20reappear%2C%20in%20the%20opposite%20order%2C%20*about%20the%20rotating%20axes*.%20We%20will%20come%20back%20to%20that.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Determination%20of%20the%20rotation%20matrix%20using%20direction%20cosines%0A%0A%20%20%20%20As%20for%20rotations%20in%20two%20dimensions%2C%20we%20can%20calculate%20the%20rotation%20matrix%20that%20describes%20the%20rotation%20of%20the%20%24xyz%24%20(local)%20coordinate%20system%20in%20relation%20to%20the%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BXYZ%7D%24%20(Global)%20coordinate%20system%20from%20the%20direction%20cosines%20between%20the%20axes%20of%20the%20two%20coordinate%20systems%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BR_%7BGl%7D%7D%20%3D%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Ccos%5Cmathbf%7BX%7Dx%20%26%20%5Ccos%5Cmathbf%7BX%7Dy%20%26%20%5Ccos%5Cmathbf%7BX%7Dz%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Ccos%5Cmathbf%7BY%7Dx%20%26%20%5Ccos%5Cmathbf%7BY%7Dy%20%26%20%5Ccos%5Cmathbf%7BY%7Dz%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Ccos%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7Dx%20%26%20%5Ccos%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7Dy%20%26%20%5Ccos%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7Dz%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Note%2C%20however%2C%20that%20for%20rotations%20about%20more%20than%20one%20axis%20these%20angles%20do%20not%20lie%20in%20the%20main%20planes%20(%24%5Cmathbf%7BXY%2C%20YZ%2C%20ZX%7D%24)%20of%20the%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BXYZ%7D%24%20coordinate%20system%2C%20as%20illustrated%20in%20the%20figure%20below%20for%20the%20direction%20angles%20of%20the%20%24y%24%20axis%20alone.%20Determining%20these%20angles%20by%20simple%20inspection%2C% 4%2C%20%24%5Cmathbf%7Bm_2%7D%24%2C%20%24%5Cmathbf%7Bm_3%7D%24%2C%20a%20basis%20of%20three%20orthogonal%20versors%20can%20be%20found%20as%20follows%20(see%20%5BDetermination%20of%20a%20coordinate%20system%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fcoordinate_system.py)%20for%20this%20recipe%20in%20detail)%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20-%20First%20axis%2C%20%24%5Cmathbf%7Bv_1%7D%24%3A%20the%20vector%20%24%5Cmathbf%7Bm_2%7D-%5Cmathbf%7Bm_1%7D%24.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20Second%20axis%2C%20%24%5Cmathbf%7Bv_2%7D%24%3A%20the%20cross%20product%20between%20the%20vectors%20%24%5Cmathbf%7Bv_1%7D%24%20and%20%24%5Cmathbf%7Bm_3%7D-%5Cmathbf%7Bm_1%7D%24.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20Third%20axis%2C%20%24%5Cmathbf%7Bv_3%7D%24%3A%20the%20cross%20product%20between%20the%20vectors%20%24%5Cmathbf%7Bv_1%7D%24%20and%20%24%5Cmathbf%7Bv_2%7D%24.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Each%20of%20these%20vectors%20is%20then%20normalized%2C%20resulting%20in%20three%20orthogonal%20versors.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20For%20example%2C%20given%20the%20positions%20%24%5Cmathbf%7Bm_1%7D%20%3D%20%5B1%2C0%2C0%5D%24%2C%20%24%5Cmathbf%7Bm_2%7D%20%3D%20%5B0%2C1%2C0%5D%24%2C%20%24%5Cmathbf%7Bm_3%7D%20%3D%20%5B0%2C0%2C1%5D%24%2C%20a%20basis%20can%20be%20found%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(np)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20m1%20%3D%20np.array(%5B1%2C%200%2C%200%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20m2%20%3D%20np.array(%5B0%2C%201%2C%200%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20m3%20%3D%20np.array(%5B0%2C%200%2C%201%5D)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20v1%20%3D%20m2%20-%20m1%0A%20%20%20%20v2%20%3D%20np.cross(v1%2C%20m3%20-%20m1)%0A%20%20%20%20v3%20%3D%20np.cross(v1%2C%20v2)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20v1%20%3D%20v1%20%2F%20np.linalg.norm(v1)%0A%20%20%20%20v2%20%3D%20v2%20%2F%20np.linalg.norm(v2)%0A%20%20%20%20v3%20%3D%20v3%20%2F%20np.linalg.norm(v3)%0A%20%20%20%20print(%22Versors%3A%22%2C%20%22%5Cnv1%20%3D%22%2C%20v1%2C%20%22%5Cnv2%20%3D%22%2C%20v2%2C%20%22%5Cnv3%20%3D%22%2C%20v3)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_RGl%20%3D%20np.array(%5Bv1%2C%20v2%2C%20v3%5D).T%20%20%23%20or%20np.vstack((v1%2C%20v2%2C%20v3)).T%0A%20%20%20%20print(%22%5CnRotation%20matrix%20RGl%3A%5Cn%22%2C%20_RGl)%0A%20%20%20%20return%20v1%2C%20v2%2C%20v3%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20A%20rotation%20matrix%20is%20not%20just%20any%20matrix.%20Its%20columns%20are%20orthogonal%20versors%2C%20so%20it%20is%20**orthonormal**%3A%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D%5ET%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D%20%3D%20%5Cmathbf%7BI%7D%24%2C%20which%20means%20that%20its%20inverse%20is%20its%20transpose.%20And%20because%20the%20basis%20is%20right-handed%2C%20its%20determinant%20is%20%24%2B1%24.%20Let's%20check%20both%2C%20together%20with%20the%20norms%20and%20the%20dot%20products%20of%20the%20versors%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(np%2C%20v1%2C%20v2%2C%20v3)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_RGl%20%3D%20np.array(%5Bv1%2C%20v2%2C%20v3%5D).T%0A%0A%20%20%20%20print(%22Norm%20of%20each%20versor%3A%22%2C%20np.linalg.norm(v1)%2C%20np.linalg.norm(v2)%2C%20np.linalg.norm(v3))%0A%20%20%20%20print(f%22Dot%20products%3A%20v1.v2%20%3D%20%7Bnp.dot(v1%2C%20v2)%3A.1e%7D%2C%20v1.v3%20%3D%20%7Bnp.dot(v1%2C%20v3)%3A.1e%7D%2C%20v2.v3%20%3D%20%7Bnp.dot(v2%2C%20v3)%3A.1e%7D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20print(%22%5CnRGl%5ET%20RGl%20%3D%5Cn%22%2C%20(_RGl.T%20%40%20_RGl).round(10)%20%2B%200.0)%0A%20%20%20%20print(f%22%5Cndet(RGl)%20%3D%20%7Bnp.linalg.det(_RGl)%3Ag%7D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20However%2C%20we%20have%20the%20same%20problem%20as%20with%20the%20rotation%20matrix%20deduced%20from%20the%20direction%20cosines%3A%20there%20is%20no%20simple%20way%20to%20read%20angles%20of%20rotation%20off%20this%20matrix.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Exercise%202.**%20Which%20of%20the%20following%20matrices%20are%20rotation%20matrices%3F%20For%20those%20that%20are%2C%20find%20the%20axis%20and%20the%20angle%20of%20the%20rotation%20by%20inspection.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BA%7D%20%3D%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%200%20%26%201%20%26%200%20%5C%5C%201%20%26%200%20%26%200%20%5C%5C%200%20%26%200%20%26%201%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%2C%20%5Cquad%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BB%7D%20%3D%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%200%20%26%20-1%20%26%200%20%5C%5C%201%20%26%200%20%26%200%20%5C%5C%200%20%26%200%20%26%201%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%2C%20%5Cquad%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BC%7D%20%3D%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%201%20%26%200%20%26%200%20%5C%5C%200%20%26%200.8%20%26%20-0.6%20%5C%5C%200%20%26%200.6%20%26%200.8%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%2C%20%5Cquad%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BD%7D%20%3D%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%201%20%26%200.1%20%26%200%20%5C%5C%200%20%26%201%20%26%200%20%5C%5C%200%20%26%200%20%26%201%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%20details%20%7C%20Solution%20to%20Exercise%202%0A%20%20%20%20A%20rotation%20matrix%20needs%20both%20properties%3A%20orthonormal%20columns%20and%20a%20determinant%20of%20%24%2B1%24.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20-%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BA%7D%24%20has%20orthonormal%20columns%2C%20but%20its%20determinant%20is%20%24-1%24.%20It%20swaps%20the%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BX%7D%24%20and%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BY%7D%24%20axes%2C%20a%20reflection%20in%20the%20plane%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BX%7D%20%3D%20%5Cmathbf%7BY%7D%24%2C%20which%20would%20turn%20a%20right-handed%20coordinate%20system%20into%20a%20left-handed%20one.%20Not%20a%20rotation.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BB%7D%24%20is%20orthonormal%20with%20determinant%20%24%2B1%24.%20Its%20third%20column%20is%20%24%5B0%2C%200%2C%201%5D%24%2C%20so%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7D%24%20is%20unchanged%20and%20the%20axis%20is%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7D%24.%20Its%20first%20column%2C%20the%20image%20of%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BX%7D%24%2C%20is%20%24%5B0%2C%201%2C%200%5D%24%3A%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BX%7D%24%20was%20turned%20into%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BY%7D%24%2C%20a%20rotation%20of%20%24%2B90%5Eo%24%20about%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7D%24.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BC%7D%24%20is%20orthonormal%20with%20determinant%20%240.8%5E2%20%2B%200.6%5E2%20%3D%201%24.%20Its%20first%20column%20is%20%24%5B1%2C%200%2C%200%5D%24%2C%20so%20the%20axis%20is%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BX%7D%24%2C%20and%20comparing%20it%20with%20the%20elemental%20rotation%20about%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BX%7D%24%2C%20%24%5Ccos%5Calpha%20%3D%200.8%24%20and%20%24%5Csin%5Calpha%20%3D%200.6%24%3A%20%24%5Calpha%20%3D%20%5Carctan2(0.6%2C%200.8)%20%3D%2036.87%5Eo%24.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BD%7D%24%20has%20determinant%20%24%2B1%24%2C%20but%20it%20is%20not%20orthonormal%3A%20its%20second%20column%2C%20%24%5B0.1%2C%201%2C%200%5D%24%2C%20has%20norm%20%24%5Csqrt%7B1.01%7D%24%20and%20is%20not%20perpendicular%20to%20the%20first.%20It%20is%20a%20shear%2C%20which%20changes%20angles%20and%20lengths.%20A%20determinant%20of%20%24%2B1%24%20alone%20is%20not%20enough.%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Euler%20angles%0A%0A%20%20%20%20There%20are%20different%20ways%20to%20describe%20a%20three-dimensional%20rotation%20of%20a%20rigid%20body%20(or%20of%20a%20coordinate%20system).%20The%20most%20straightforward%20would%20probably%20be%20spherical%20coordinates%2C%20but%20it%20would%20be%20difficult%20to%20give%20them%20an%20anatomical%20or%20clinical%20interpretation.%20The%20solution%20most%20often%20employed%20in%20biomechanics%20is%20Euler%20angles.%20Under%20certain%20conditions%20Euler%20angles%20have%20an%20anatomical%20interpretation%2C%20but%20the%20representation%20also%20has%20caveats%2C%20as%20we%20will%20see.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20In%20the%2018th%20century%2C%20%5BLeonhard%20Euler%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FLeonhard_Euler)%20showed%20that%20two%20three-dimensional%20coordinate%20systems%20with%20a%20common%20origin%20can%20be%20related%20by%20a%20sequence%20of%20up%20to%20three%20elemental%20rotations%20about%20the%20axes%20of%20the%20local%20coordinate%20system%2C%20where%20no%20two%20successive%20rotations%20may%20be%20about%20the%20same%20axis.%20The%20angles%20of%20these%20rotations%20are%20now%20known%20as%20%5BEuler%20(or%20Eulerian)%20angles%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FEuler_angles).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cfigure%20aria-describedby%3D%22figure-caption-5%22%3E%3Ccenter%3E%3Cimg%20src%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fupload.wikimedia.org%2Fwikipedia%2Fcommons%2F8%2F85%2FEuler2a.gif%22%20width%3D300%20alt%3D%22Euler%20angles%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fcenter%3E%3C%2Ffigure%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cspan%20id%3D%22figure-caption-5%22%20class%3D%22figure-caption%22%20style%3D%22display%3Ablock%3Btext-align%3Acenter%3Bfont-style%3Aitalic%22%3EFigure.%20Euler%20angles%3A%20a%20way%20to%20reach%20any%20orientation%20using%20a%20specific%20sequence%20of%20elemental%20rotations%20(%3Ca%20href%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FEuler_angles%22%3Eimage%20from%20Wikipedia%3C%2Fa%3E).%3C%2Fspan%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Elemental%20rotations%0A%0A%20%20%20%20First%2C%20let's%20look%20at%20rotations%20about%20a%20fixed%20Global%20coordinate%20system%2C%20as%20we%20did%20in%20two%20dimensions.%20The%20next%20figure%20illustrates%20elemental%20rotations%20of%20the%20local%20coordinate%20system%20about%20each%20axis%20of%20the%20fixed%20Global%20coordinate%20system.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cfigure%20aria-describedby%3D%22figure-caption-6%22%3E%3Ccenter%3E%3Cimg%20src%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fimages%2Frotations.png%3Fraw%3D1%22%20width%3D700%20alt%3D%22elemental%20rotations%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fcenter%3E%3C%2Ffigure%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cspan%20id%3D%22figure-caption-6%22%20class%3D%22figure-caption%22%20style%3D%22display%3Ablock%3Btext-align%3Acenter%3Bfont-style%3Aitalic%22%3EFigure.%20Elemental%20rotations%20of%20the%20%24xyz%24%20coordinate%20system%20about%20each%20axis%2C%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BX%7D%24%2C%20%24%5Cmathbf%7 %7D%24%20to%20the%20right%2C%20the%20convention%20recommended%20for%20motion%20analysis%20by%20the%20International%20Society%20of%20Biomechanics%20(Wu%20%26%20Cavanagh%2C%201995).%20We%20follow%20two%20vectors%20attached%20to%20the%20right%20arm%3A%20its%20long%20axis%2C%20pointing%20from%20the%20shoulder%20down%20to%20the%20hand%2C%20%24%5B0%2C%20-1%2C%200%5D%24%3B%20and%20the%20direction%20the%20palm%20faces%2C%20initially%20towards%20the%20thigh%2C%20%24%5B0%2C%200%2C%20-1%5D%24.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20three%20movements%20are%20rotations%20about%20fixed%20axes%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20Flexion%3A%20the%20arm%20swings%20forward%20and%20up%2C%20a%20rotation%20of%20%24%2B90%5Eo%24%20about%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7D%24.%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Horizontal%20abduction%3A%20the%20arm%20swings%20from%20the%20front%20to%20the%20side%2C%20a%20rotation%20of%20%24-90%5Eo%24%20about%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BY%7D%24.%0A%20%20%20%203.%20Adduction%3A%20the%20arm%20comes%20down%20from%20the%20side%2C%20a%20rotation%20of%20%24%2B90%5Eo%24%20about%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BX%7D%24.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Before%20you%20run%20the%20next%20cell**%2C%20check%20those%20signs%20with%20the%20right-hand%20rule%2C%20and%20predict%20where%20the%20palm%20faces%20at%20the%20end.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(np)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_arm%20%3D%20np.array(%5B0%2C%20-1%2C%200%5D)%20%20%23%20long%20axis%20of%20the%20arm%2C%20from%20the%20shoulder%20to%20the%20hand%0A%20%20%20%20_palm%20%3D%20np.array(%5B0%2C%200%2C%20-1%5D)%20%20%23%20the%20right%20palm%2C%20facing%20the%20thigh%0A%20%20%20%20_steps%20%3D%20%5B%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20(%22flexion%2C%20%2B90%20about%20Z%22%2C%20rotZ(90))%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20(%22horizontal%20abduction%2C%20-90%20about%20Y%22%2C%20rotY(-90))%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20(%22adduction%2C%20%2B90%20about%20X%22%2C%20rotX(90))%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%5D%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_R%20%3D%20np.eye(3)%0A%20%20%20%20for%20_name%2C%20_Ri%20in%20_steps%3A%0A%20%20%20 0the%20humerus%20depends%20on%20the%20path%20the%20arm%20took%20to%20reach%20a%20position%2C%20and%20that%20a%20description%20of%20the%20arm's%20orientation%20by%20three%20angles%20depends%20on%20the%20order%20in%20which%20the%20angles%20are%20defined.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Guiding%20questions%202.**%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20Problem%206%20asks%20you%20to%20compute%20the%20order%20you%20tried%20in%20Guiding%20question%200.2.%20Before%20computing%2C%20predict%3A%20will%20the%20palm%20end%20up%20facing%20forward%20again%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Why%20did%20the%20second%20movement%20change%20the%20direction%20of%20the%20palm%2C%20while%20the%20first%20one%20did%20not%3F%0A%20%20%20%203.%20A%20colleague%20reports%20the%20arm's%20orientation%20as%20the%20sum%20of%20the%20three%20angles%20about%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BX%7D%24%2C%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BY%7D%24%20and%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7D%24.%20What%20would%20that%20sum%20be%20for%20Codman's%20movement%2C%20and%20what%20is%20wrong%20with%20it%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20One%20rotation%20is%20enough%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Codman's%20three%20rotations%20turned%20out%20to%20be%20a%20single%20rotation%20about%20one%20axis.%20That%20is%20not%20a%20coincidence%20of%20the%20example.%20Euler's%20rotation%20theorem%20says%20that%20*any*%20rotation%20matrix%20is%20a%20single%20rotation%2C%20by%20some%20angle%20%24%5Ctheta%24%2C%20about%20some%20axis%20%24%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bn%7D%7D%24.%20Both%20can%20be%20read%20off%20the%20matrix.%20The%20trace%20(the%20sum%20of%20the%20diagonal)%20gives%20the%20angle%2C%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathrm%7Btr%7D(%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D)%20%3D%201%20%2B%202%5Ccos%5Ctheta%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20and%20the%20antisymmetric%20part%20of%20the%20matrix%20gives%20the%20axis%2C%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%20R_%7B21%7D%20-%20R_%7B12%7D%20%5C%5C%20R_%7B02 between%20%240%5Eo%24%20and%20%24180%5Eo%24%2C%20and%20lets%20the%20direction%20of%20the%20axis%20carry%20the%20sign.%20And%20rotations%20of%20%2430%5Eo%24%2C%20%2445%5Eo%24%20and%20%2460%5Eo%24%20add%20up%20to%20a%20single%20rotation%20of%20%2469.4%5Eo%24%2C%20not%20%24135%5Eo%24.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Unlike%20the%20three%20Euler%20angles%2C%20this%20angle%20does%20not%20depend%20on%20any%20convention%3A%20whatever%20sequence%20you%20choose%20to%20describe%20the%20orientation%2C%20the%20single%20equivalent%20rotation%20is%20the%20same.%20It%20is%20the%20rotational%20part%20of%20the%20helical%20(or%20screw)%20axis%20used%20to%20describe%20joint%20motion%2C%20and%20a%20convenient%2C%20sequence-free%20answer%20to%20the%20question%20%22how%20much%20did%20this%20segment%20rotate%3F%22.%20Problem%2010%20asks%20you%20to%20go%20the%20other%20way%2C%20from%20an%20axis%20and%20an%20angle%20to%20the%20rotation%20matrix.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20How%20much%20does%20the%20order%20matter%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Two%20quarter%20turns%20about%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7D%24%20and%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BX%7D%24%20ended%20in%20completely%20different%20places%20depending%20on%20their%20order.%20Are%20joint%20angles%20of%20a%20few%20degrees%20just%20as%20sensitive%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Before%20you%20run%20the%20next%20cell**%2C%20predict%3A%20one%20body%20is%20turned%20by%20%2410%5Eo%24%20about%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7D%24%20and%20then%20by%20%2410%5Eo%24%20about%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BX%7D%24%2C%20and%20another%20body%20by%20the%20same%20two%20rotations%20in%20the%20opposite%20order.%20By%20how%20much%20do%20their%20final%20orientations%20differ%3F%20And%20for%20%2445%5Eo%24%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20difference%20between%20two%20orientations%20is%20itself%20a%20rotation%2C%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BR_1%5ET%7D%5Cmathbf%7BR_2%7D%24%2C%20and%20%60axis_angle%60%20measures%20it%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_()%3A%0A%20%20%20%20print(%22%20angle%20%20%20%20Z%20then%20X%20vs%20X%20then%20Z%3A%20differ%20by%20%20%20%20axis%20of%20the%20difference%22)%0A%20%20%20%20for%20_theta%20in%20%5B1%2C%205%2C%2010%2C%2020%2C%2045%2C%2090%5D%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_z_then_x%20%3D%20rotX(_theta)%20%40%20rotZ(_theta)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_x_then_z%20%3D%20rotZ(_theta)%20%40%20rotX(_theta)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_axis%2C%20_diff%20%3D%20axis_angle(_z_then_x.T%20%40%20_x_then_z)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20print(f%22%7B_theta%3A5d%7D%20%20%20%20%7B_diff%3A10.3f%7D%20degrees%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%7B_axis.round(2)%20%2B%200.0%7D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20For%20rotations%20of%20%241%5Eo%24%2C%20the%20two%20orders%20end%20within%20%240.02%5Eo%24%20of%20each%20other%3B%20for%20%2410%5Eo%24%2C%20within%20%241.7%5Eo%24%3B%20for%20%2420%5Eo%24%2C%20%246.9%5Eo%24%3B%20for%20%2445%5Eo%24%2C%20%2434%5Eo%24%3B%20and%20the%20two%20quarter%20turns%20end%20%24120%5Eo%24%20apart.%20The%20difference%20grows%20roughly%20with%20the%20square%20of%20the%20angle%3A%20ten%20times%20the%20angle%2C%20a%20hundred%20times%20the%20difference.%20For%20small%20angles%20it%20is%20a%20rotation%20about%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BY%7D%24%2C%20the%20axis%20perpendicular%20to%20the%20two%20that%20were%20used%3B%20Problem%2011%20asks%20you%20to%20show%20why.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Small%20rotations%20nearly%20commute.%20That%20is%20why%2C%20for%20a%20joint%20that%20moves%20little%20outside%20its%20main%20plane%2C%20different%20sequences%20of%20Euler%20angles%20give%20nearly%20the%20same%20angles%2C%20and%20why%20the%20choice%20of%20sequence%20matters%20most%20for%20large%20three-dimensional%20movements%2C%20such%20as%20those%20of%20the%20shoulder%20or%20of%20the%20hip%20in%20sport.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20The%2012%20different%20sequences%20of%20Euler%20angles%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20Euler%20angles%20are%20defined%20in%20terms%20of%20rotations%20about%20a%20rotating%20local%20coordinate%20system.%20As%20we%20saw%20for%20the%20sequence%20of%20rotations%20about%20%24x%2C%20y%2C%20z%24%2C%20the%20axes%20of%20the%20local%20coordinate%20system%20are%20not%20fixed%20in%20space%3A%20after%20the%20first%20elemental%20rotation%2C%20the%20other%20two%20axes%20have%20moved.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Other%20sequences%20of%20rotations%20can%20be%20formed%20without%20mixing%20axes%20of%20the%20two%20coordinate%20systems%20(Global%20and%20local)%20as%20rotation%20axes.%20There%20are%2012%20valid%20sequences%20of%20three%20elemental%20rotations%20that%20can%20describe%20the%20rotation%20of%20a%20coordinate%20system%20with%20respect%20to%20another%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Barray%7D%7Bll%7D%0A%20%20%20%20xyz%20%5Cquad%20xzy%20%5Cquad%20yzx%20%5Cquad%20yxz%20%5Cquad%20zxy%20%5Cquad%20zyx%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20xyx%20%5Cquad%20xzx%20%5Cquad%20yzy%20%5Cquad%20yxy%20%5Cquad%20zxz%20%5Cquad%20zyz%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Barray%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20first%20six%20sequences%20(first%20row)%20are%20about%20three%20different%20axes%20and%20are%20usually%20referred%20to%20as%20Cardan%20or%20Tait%E2%80%93Bryan%20angles.%20The%20other%20six%20(second%20row)%20have%20the%20first%20and%20third%20rotations%20about%20the%20same%20axis%2C%20but%20keep%20in%20mind%20that%20the%20axis%20of%20the%20third%20rotation%20is%20no%20longer%20where%20it%20was%2C%20because%20it%20changed%20orientation%20with%20the%20second%20rotation.%20The%20sequences%20with%20a%20repeated%20axis%20are%20known%20as%20proper%20or%20classic%20Euler%20angles.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Which%20order%20to%20use%20is%20a%20matter%20of%20convention%2C%20but%20because%20the%20order%20affects%20the%20results%2C%20it%20is%20fundamental%20to%20follow%20a%20convention%20and%20to%20report%20it.%20In%20engineering%20mechanics%20(including%20biomechanics)%2C%20the%20%24xyz%24%20order%20is%20more%20common%3B%20in%20physics%2C%20the%20%24zxz%24%20order%20is%20more%20common%20(but%20the%20letters%20chosen%20for%20the%20axes%20are%20arbitrary%3B%20what%20matters%20is%20the%20directions%20they%20represent).%20In%20biomechanics%2C%20the%20order%20of%20the%20Cardan%20angles%20is%20most%20often%20based%20on%20the%20angle%20of%20most%20interest%20or%20of%20most%20reliable%20measurement.%20Accordingly%2C%20the%20axis%20of%20flexion%E2%80%93extension%20is%20typically%20the%20first%20axis%2C%20the%20axis%20of%20abduction%E2%80%93adduction%20the%20second%2C%20and%20the%20axis%20of%20internal%E2%80%93external%20rotation%20the%20last%20one%3B%20for%20the%20knee%2C%20this%20is%20the%20order%20of%20the%20joint%20coordinate%20system%20of%20Grood%20and%20Suntay%20(1983).%20The%20%24zyx%24%20order%20is%20commonly%20used%20to%20describe%20the%20orientation%20of%20a%20ship%20or%20an%20aircraft%2C%20and%20the%20rotations%20are%20known%20as%20the%20nautical%20angles%3A%20yaw%2C%20pitch%20and%20roll%2C%20respectively%20(see%20next%20figure).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cfigure%20aria-describedby%3D%22figure-caption-9%22%3E%3Ccenter%3E%3Cimg%20src%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fupload.wikimedia.org%2Fwikipedia%2Fcommons%2Fthumb%2F1%2F16%2FYaw_Axis.svg%2F330px-Yaw_Axis.svg.png%22%20width%3D320%20alt%3D%22principal%20axes%20of%20an%20aircraft%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fcenter%3E%3C%2Ffigure%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cspan%20id%3D%22figure-caption-9%22%20class%3D%22figure-caption%22%20style%3D%22display%3Ablock%3Btext-align%3Acenter%3Bfont-style%3Aitalic%22%3EFigure.%20The%20principal%20axes%20of%20an%20aircraft%20and%20the%20names%20of%20the%20rotations%20about%20them%20(%3Ca%20href%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FEuler_angles%22%3Eimage%20from%20Wikipedia%3C%2Fa%3E).%3C%2Fspan%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20If%2C%20instead%20of%20rotations%20about%20the%20rotating%20local%20coordinate%20system%2C%20we%20perform%20rotations%20about%20the%20fixed%20Global%20coordinate%20system%2C%20we%20have%20another%2012%20sequences%20of%20three%20elemental%20rotations%2C%20called%20simply%20rotation%20angles.%20In%20total%20there%20are%2024%20possible%20sequences%2C%20but%20they%20are%20not%20independent%3A%20with%20the%2012%20sequences%20of%20Euler%20angles%20in%20the%20local%20coordinate%20system%20we%20can%20obtain%20the%20other%2012%20in%20the%20Global%20coordinate%20system.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20function%20below%20determines%20the%20rotation%20matrix%20in%20algebraic%20form%20for%20any%20of%20the%2024%20sequences%20(sequences%20of%20only%20one%20or%20two%20axes%20can%20also%20be%20entered)%2C%20and%20in%20numerical%20form%20if%20a%20list%20of%20angles%20is%20given.%20It%20is%20a%20compact%20version%20of%20the%20function%20%60euler_rotmat.py%60%2C%20from%20the%20%60functions%60%20folder%20of%20this%20repository.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.function%0Adef%20euler_rotmat(order%3D%22xyz%22%2C%20frame%3D%22local%22%2C%20angles%3DNone%2C%20unit%3D%22deg%22)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22Rotation%20matrix%20for%20a%20sequence%20of%20up%20to%20three%20elemental%20rotations.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%60order%60%20is%20a%20string%20of%20one%20to%20three%20letters%20among%20x%2C%20y%20and%20z%3B%20the%20first%0A%20%20%20%20letter%20is%20the%20first%20rotation.%20With%20frame%3D%22local%22%2C%20the%20rotations%20are%20about%0A%20%20%20%20the%20axes%20of%20the%20rotating%20coordinate%20system%20(Euler%20angles)%20and%20the%20matrix%20is%0A%20%20%20%20Global-to-local%3B%20with%20frame%3D%22global%22%2C%20they%20are%20about%20the%20fixed%20axes%20and%20the%0A%20%20%20%20matrix%20is%20local-to-Global.%20The%20angles%20of%20the%20first%2C%20second%20and%20third%0A%20%20%20%20rotations%20are%20the%20symbols%20alpha%2C%20beta%20and%20gamma.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Returns%20the%20algebraic%20matrix%20and%2C%20if%20%60angles%60%20is%20given%2C%20also%20the%20matrix%20with%0A%20%20%20%20those%20values%20substituted%20(use%20None%20for%20an%20angle%20that%20stays%20symbolic).%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20import%20sympy%20as%20sym%0A%0A%20%20%20%20cos%2C%20sin%20%3D%20sym.cos%2C%20sym.sin%0A%20%20%20%20symbols%20%3D%20sym.symbols(%22alpha%2C%20beta%2C%20gamma%22)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20def%20elemental(axis%2C%20q)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20R%20%3D%20%7B%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22x%22%3A%20sym.Matrix(%5B%5B1%2C%200%2C%200%5D%2C%20%5B0%2C%20cos(q)%2C%20sin(q)%5D%2C%20%5B0%2C%20-sin(q)%2C%20cos(q)%5D%5D)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22y%22%3A%20sym.Matrix(%5B%5Bcos(q)%2C%200%2C%20-sin(q)%5D%2C%20%5B0%2C%201%2C%200%5D%2C%20%5Bsin(q)%2C%200%2C%20cos(q)%5D%5D)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22z%22%3A%20sym.Matrix(%5B%5Bcos(q)%2C%20sin(q)%2C%200%5D%2C%20%5B-sin(q)%2C%20cos(q)%2C%200%5D%2C%20%5B0%2C%200%2C%201%5D%5D)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%7D%5Baxis%5D%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20return%20R.T%20if%20frame.lower()%20%3D%3D%20%22global%22%20else%20R%0A%0A%20%20%20%20R%20%3D%20sym.eye(3)%0A%20%20%20%20for%20axis%2C%20q%20in%20zip(order.lower()%2C%20symbols)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20R%20%3D%20elemental(axis%2C%20q)%20*%20R%20%20%23%20the%20matrix%20product%20goes%20from%20right%20to%20left%0A%20%20%20%20if%20angles%20is%20None%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20return%20R%0A%0A%20%20%20%20values%20%3D%20%7B%7D%0A%20%20%20%20for%20q%2C%20angle%20in%20zip(symbols%2C%20angles)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20if%20angle%20is%20not%20None%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20values%5Bq%5D%20%3D%20sym.rad(angle)%20if%20unit%5B%3A3%5D.lower()%20%3D%3D%20%22deg%22%20else%20angle%0A%20%20%20%20return%20R%2C%20sym.simplify(R.subs(values))%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20For%20instance%2C%20here%20are%20the%20rotation%20matrix%20in%20algebraic%20form%20for%20the%20%24zxz%24%20order%20of%20Euler% al%20(fixed)%20%24XYZ%24%20coordinate%20system%20is%20shown%20in%20green%2C%20the%20local%20(rotating)%20%24xyz%24%20coordinate%20system%20in%20blue.%20The%20nodal%20axis%20(%3Cb%3EN%3C%2Fb%3E%2C%20in%20red)%20is%20defined%20by%20the%20intersection%20of%20the%20%24YZ%24%20and%20%24xy%24%20planes%2C%20and%20all%20rotations%20can%20be%20described%20in%20relation%20to%20this%20nodal%20axis%20or%20to%20an%20axis%20perpendicular%20to%20it.%20Second%20row%3A%20starting%20from%20no%20rotation%2C%20the%20local%20coordinate%20system%20is%20rotated%20by%20%24%5Calpha%24%20about%20the%20%24x%24%20axis%2C%20then%20by%20%24%5Cbeta%24%20about%20the%20rotated%20%24y%24%20axis%2C%20and%20finally%20by%20%24%5Cgamma%24%20about%20the%20twice-rotated%20%24z%24%20axis.%20The%20line%20of%20nodes%20coincides%20with%20the%20%24y%24%20axis%20of%20the%20second%20rotation.%3C%2Fspan%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Determination%20of%20the%20Euler%20angles%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Once%20a%20convention%20is%20adopted%2C%20the%20corresponding%20three%20Euler%20angles%20can%20be%20found%20from%20the%20rotation%20matrix.%20For%20example%2C%20for%20the%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D_%7Bxyz%7D%24%20rotation%20matrix%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_()%3A%0A%20%20%20%20show_matrix(r%22%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D_%7Blocal%7D(x%3A%5Calpha%2C%20y%3A%5Cbeta%2C%20z%3A%5Cgamma)%22%2C%20euler_rotmat(order%3D%22xyz%22%2C%20frame%3D%22local%22))%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20The%20corresponding%20Cardan%20angles%20for%20the%20%24xyz%24%20sequence%20are%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Barray%7D%7Bll%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Calpha%20%3D%20%5Carctan%5Cleft(%5Cdfrac%7B%5Csin(%5Calpha)%7D%7B%5Ccos(%5Calpha)%7D%5Cright)%20%3D%20%5Carctan%5Cleft(%5Cdfrac%7B-%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D_%7B21%7D%7D%7B%5C%3B%5C%3B%5C%3B%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D_%7B22%7D%7D%5Cright)%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbeta%20%3D%20%5Carctan%5Cleft(%5Cdfrac%7B%5Csin(%5Cbeta)%7D%7B%5Ccos(%5Cbeta)%7D%5Cright)%20%3D%20%5Carctan%5Cleft(%5Cdfrac%7B%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D_%7B20%7D%7D%7B%5Csqrt%7B%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D_%7B00%7D%5E2%2B%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D_%7B10%7D%5E2%7D%7D%5Cright)%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cgamma%20%3D%20%5Carctan%5Cleft(%5Cdfrac%7B%5Csin(%5Cgamma)%7D%7B%5Ccos(%5Cgamma)%7D%5Cright)%20%3D%20%5Carctan%5Cleft(%5Cdfrac%7B-%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D_%7B10%7D%7D%7B%5C%3B%5C%3B%5C%3B%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D_%7B00%7D%7D%5Cright)%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Barray%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20(with%20the%20rows%20and%20columns%20numbered%20from%200%2C%20as%20in%20Python).%20We%20use%20the%20function%20%60arctan2%60%20rather%20than%20%60arcsin%60%2C%20%60arccos%60%20or%20%60arctan%60%2C%20because%20those%20cannot%2C%20for%20example%2C%20distinguish%20%2445%5Eo%24%20from%20%24135%5Eo%24%2C%20and%20for%20better%20numerical%20accuracy%3B%20see%20%5BAngular%20kinematics%20in%20a%20plane%20(2D)%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fkinematics_angular_2d.py)%20for%20more%20on%20these%20issues.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Here%20is%20a%20Python%20function%20that%20computes%20the%20Euler%20angles%20of%20the%20rotation%20from%20the%20Global%20to%20the%20local%20coordinate%20system%20for%20the%20%24xyz%24%20Cardan%20sequence%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.function%0Adef%20euler_angles_from_rot_xyz(rot_matrix%2C%20unit%3D%22deg%22)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22Compute%20Euler%20angles%20from%20rotation%20matrix%20in%20the%20xyz%20sequence.%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20import%20numpy%20as%20np%0A%0A%20%20%20%20R%20%3D%20np.asarray(rot_matrix%2C%20dtype%3Dnp.float64)%5B%3A3%2C%20%3A3%5D%0A%20%20%20%20angles%20%3D%20np.zeros(3)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20angles%5B0%5D%20%3D%20np.arctan2(-R%5B2%2C%201%5D%2C%20R%5B2%2C%202%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20angles%5B1%5D%20%3D%20np.arctan2(R%5B2%2C%200%5D%2C%20np.sqrt(R%5B0%2C%200%5D%20**%202%20%2B%20R%5B1%2C%200%5D%20**%202))%0A%20%20%20%20angles%5B2%5D%20%3D%20np.arctan2(-R%5B1%2C%200%5D%2C%20R%5B0%2C%200%5D)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20if%20unit%5B%3A3%5D.lower()%20%3D%3D%20%22deg%22%3A%20%20%23%20convert%20from%20rad%20to%20degree%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20angles%20%3D%20np.rad2deg(angles)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20return%20angles%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20For%20instance%2C%20consider%20sequential%20rotations%20of%20%2445%5Eo%24%20about%20%24x%24%2C%20%24y%24%2C%20%24z%24.%20The%20resulting%20rotation%20matrix%20is%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_()%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_Ra%2C%20Rn45%20%3D%20euler_rotmat(order%3D%22xyz%22%2C%20frame%3D%22local%22%2C%20angles%3D%5B45%2C%2045%2C%2045%5D)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20show_matrix(r%22%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D_%7Blocal%7D(x%3A45%5Eo%2C%20y%3A45%5Eo%2C%20z%3A45%5Eo)%22%2C%20Rn45%2C%20digits%3D4)%0A%20%20%20%20return%20(Rn45%2C)%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20Let's%20check%20by%20calculating%20the%20Cardan%20angles%20back%20from%20this%20rotation%20matrix%20with%20%60euler_angles_from_rot_xyz()%60%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(Rn45)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20euler_angles_from_rot_xyz(Rn45%2C%20unit%3D%22deg%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20We%20could%20implement%20a%20function%20to%20calculate%20the%20Euler%20angles%20for%20each%20of%20the%2012%20sequences%20(24%2C%20counting%20the%20rotations%20from%20and%20to%20both%20coordinate%20systems)%2C%20but%20this%20is%20tedious.%20There%20is%20a%20smarter%20solution%20using%20the%20concept%20of%20%5Bquaternion%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FQuaternion)%2C%20but%20we%20will%20not%20see%20it%20here.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Exercise%204.**%20The%20round%20trip%20gave%20back%20the%20angles%20we%20put%20in%2C%20but%20the%20angles%20that%20produce%20a%20given%20rotation%20matrix%20are%20not%20unique.%20The%20matrix%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D_%7Blocal%7D(x%3A10%5Eo%2C%20y%3A-30%5Eo%2C%20z%3A50%5Eo)%24%20gives%20back%20exactly%20%24(10%5Eo%2C%20-30%5Eo%2C%2050%5Eo)%24.%20Find%20another%20set%20of%20three%20%24xyz%24%20angles%20that%20produces%20the%20same%20matrix%2C%20and%20check%20it%20with%20%60euler_rotmat%60.%20(Hint%3A%20start%20by%20adding%20%24180%5Eo%24%20to%20the%20first%20and%20the%20third%20angles%2C%20and%20see%20what%20the%20second%20one%20must%20do%20to%20compensate.)%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo%2C%20np)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_%2C%20_R%20%3D%20euler_rotmat(order%3D%22xyz%22%2C%20frame%3D%22local%22%2C%20angles%3D%5B10%2C%20-30%2C%2050%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20_%2C%20_R_alt%20%3D%20euler_rotmat(order%3D%22xyz%22%2C%20frame%3D%22local%22%2C%20angles%3D%5B190%2C%20210%2C%20230%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20_same%20%3D%20np.allclose(np.array(_R%2C%20dtype%3Dfloat)%2C%20np.array(_R_alt%2C%20dtype%3Dfloat))%0A%20%20%20%20_back%20%3D%20euler_angles_from_rot_xyz(np.array(_R_alt%2C%20dtype%3Dfloat)).round(4)%20%2B%200.0%0A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.accordion(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%7B%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22Solution%20to%20Exercise%204%22%3A%20mo.md(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20rf%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20Adding%20%24180%5Eo%24%20to%20%24%5Calpha%24%20changes%20the%20sign%20of%20both%20%24%5Csin%5Calpha%24%20and%20%24%5Ccos%5Calpha%24%2C%20and%20the%20same%20for%20%24%5Cgamma%24.%20To%20compensate%2C%20the%20second%20angle%20must%20keep%20its%20sine%20and%20change%20the%20sign%20of%20its%20cosine%2C%20which%20%24180%5Eo%20-%20%5Cbeta%24%20does.%20Every%20entry%20of%20the%20matrix%20is%20then%20a%20product%20in%20which%20either%20none%20or%20exactly%20two%20of%20the%20factors%20change%20sign%2C%20so%20the%20matrix%20does%20not%20change.%20The%20second%20set%20of%20angles%20is%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20(%5Calpha%20%2B%20180%5Eo%2C%5C%3B%20180%5Eo%20-%20%5Cbeta%2C%5C%3B%20%5Cgamma%20%2B%20180%5Eo)%20%3D%20(190%5Eo%2C%5C%3B%20210%5Eo%2C%5C%3B%20230%5Eo)%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20or%2C%20written%20between%20%24-180%5Eo%24%20and%20%24180%5Eo%24%2C%20%24(-170%5Eo%2C%20-150%5Eo%2C%20-130%5Eo)%24.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Same%20matrix%3A%20%7B_same%7D.%20And%20%60euler_angles_from_rot_xyz%60%20applied%20to%20this%20matrix%20returns%20%7B_back%7D%2C%20the%20first%20solution%20again.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20function%20always%20picks%20the%20solution%20with%20%24%5Ccos%5Cbeta%20%5Cgeq%200%24%2C%20that%20is%2C%20with%20%24%5Cbeta%24%20between%20%24-90%5Eo%24%20and%20%2490%5Eo%24%2C%20because%20it%20computes%20the%20cosine%20of%20%24%5Cbeta%24%20as%20a%20positive%20square%20root.%20That%20choice%20is%20a%20convention%20too%2C%20and%20it%20is%20the%20reason%20why%20the%20second%20angle%20of%20a%20Cardan%20sequence%20is%20reported%20between%20%24-90%5Eo%24%20and%20%2490%5Eo%24.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%7D%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20Apart%20from%20that%20choice%20between%20two%20solutions%2C%20the%20round%20trip%20worked%20here.%20It%20does%20not%20always%20work%2C%20and%20the%20reason%20is%20a%20problem%20of%20Euler%20angles%20known%20as%20gimbal%20lock.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Gimbal%20lock%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%5BGimbal%20lock%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FGimbal_lock)%20is%20the%20loss%20of%20one%20degree%20of%20freedom%20that%20occurs%20when%20an%20axis%20of%20rotation%20is%20placed%20parallel%20to%20a%20previous%20axis%20of%2 Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Translation%20and%20rotation%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Consider%20the%20case%20where%20the%20local%20coordinate%20system%20is%20translated%20and%20rotated%20in%20relation%20to%20the%20Global%20coordinate%20system%2C%20as%20illustrated%20in%20the%20next%20figure.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cfigure%20aria-describedby%3D%22figure-caption-11%22%3E%3Ccenter%3E%3Cimg%20src%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fimages%2Ftransrot3D.png%3Fraw%3D1%22%20width%3D450%20alt%3D%22translation%20and%20rotation%203D%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fcenter%3E%3C%2Ffigure%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cspan%20id%3D%22figure-caption-11%22%20class%3D%22figure-caption%22%20style%3D%22display%3Ablock%3Btext-align%3Acenter%3Bfont-style%3Aitalic%22%3EFigure.%20A%20point%20in%20three-dimensional%20space%20represented%20in%20two%20coordinate%20systems%2C%20with%20one%20coordinate%20system%20translated%20and%20rotated.%3C%2Fspan%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20position%20of%20the%20point%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BP%7D%24%2C%20originally%20described%20in%20the%20local%20coordinate%20system%2C%20is%20described%20in%20the%20Global%20coordinate%20system%20in%20vector%20form%20by%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BP_G%7D%20%3D%20%5Cmathbf%7BL_G%7D%20%2B%20%5Cmathbf%7BR_%7BGl%7D%7D%5Cmathbf%7BP_l%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20This%20means%20that%20we%20first%20*disrotate*%20the%20local%20coordinate%20system%20and%20then%20correct%20for%20the%20translation%20between%20the%20two%20coordinate%20systems.%20We%20cannot%20invert%20this%20order%3A%20the%20position%20of%20the%20point%20is%20expressed%20in%20the%20local%20coordinate%20system%2C%20and%20we%20cannot%20add%20it%20to%20a%20vector%20expressed%20in%20the%20Global%20coordinate%20system%20before%20converting%20both%20vectors%20to%20the%20same%20coordinate%20system.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20To%20find%20the%20position%20of%20a%20point%20in%20the%20local%20coordinate%20system%2C%20given%20its%20position%20in%20the%20Global%20coordinate%20system%2C%20the%20rotation%20matrix%20and%20the%20translation%20vector%2C%20we%20invert%20the%20expression%20above%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Barray%7D%7Bll%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BP_G%7D%20%3D%20%5Cmathbf%7BL_G%7D%20%2B%20%5Cmathbf%7BR_%7BGl%7D%7D%5Cmathbf%7BP_l%7D%20%5Cimplies%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BR_%7BGl%7D%5E%7B-1%7D%7D%5Ccdot%5Cmathbf%7BP_G%7D%20%3D%20%5Cmathbf%7BR_%7BGl%7D%5E%7B-1%7D%7D%5Cleft(%5Cmathbf%7BL_G%7D%20%2B%20%5Cmathbf%7BR_%7BGl%7D%7D%5Cmathbf%7BP_l%7D%5Cright)%20%5Cimplies%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BR_%7BGl%7D%5E%7B-1%7D%7D%5Cmathbf%7BP_G%7D%20%3D%20%5Cmathbf%7BR_%7BGl%7D%5E%7B-1%7D%7D%5Cmathbf%7BL_G%7D%20%2B%20%5Cmathbf%7BR_%7BGl%7D%5E%7B-1%7D%7D%5Cmathbf%7BR_%7BGl%7D%7D%5Cmathbf%7BP_l%7D%20%5Cimplies%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BP_l%7D%20%3D%20%5Cmathbf%7BR_%7BGl%7D%5E%7B-1%7D%7D%5Cleft(%5Cmathbf%7BP_G%7D-%5Cmathbf%7BL_G%7D%5Cright)%20%3D%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BR_%7BGl%7D%5ET%7D%5Cleft(%5Cmathbf%7BP_G%7D-%5Cmathbf%7BL_G%7D%5Cright)%20%5C%3B%5C%3B%5C%3B%5C%3B%5C%3B%20%5Ctext%7Bor%7D%20%5C%3B%5C%3B%5C%3B%5C%3B%5C%3B%20%5Cmathbf%7BP_l%7D%20%3D%20%5Cmathbf%7BR_%7BlG%7D%7D%5Cleft(%5Cmathbf%7BP_G%7D-%5Cmathbf%7BL_G%7D%5Cright)%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Barray%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20To%20perform%20the%20inverse%20operation%2C%20from%20the%20Global%20to%20the%20local%20coordinate%20system%2C%20we%20first%20translate%20and%20then%20rotate.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Transformation%20matrix%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20translation%20and%20rotation%20operations%20can%20be%20combined%20in%20a%20single%20matrix%2C%20called%20the%20transformation%20matrix%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BP_X%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20% 20%200%20%26%200%20%26%200%20%26%201%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BP_X%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BP_Y%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathbf%7BP_Z%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%201%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Example%20with%20actual%20motion%20analysis%20data%0A%0A%20%20%20%20*The%20data%20for%20this%20example%20are%20taken%20from%20page%20183%20of%20David%20Winter's%20book.*%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Consider%20the%20following%20positions%20of%20markers%20placed%20on%20a%20leg%20(described%20in%20the%20laboratory%20coordinate%20system%20with%20coordinates%20%24x%2C%20y%2C%20z%24%20in%20cm%2C%20the%20%24x%24%20axis%20pointing%20forward%20and%20the%20%24y%24%20axis%20pointing%20upward)%3A%20lateral%20malleolus%20(**lm**%20%3D%20%5B2.92%2C%2010.10%2C%2018.85%5D)%2C%20medial%20malleolus%20(**mm**%20%3D%20%5B2.71%2C%2010.22%2C%2026.52%5D)%2C%20fibular%20head%20(**fh**%20%3D%20%5B5.05%2C%2041.90%2C%2015.41%5D)%20and%20medial%20condyle%20(**mc**%20%3D%20%5B8.29%2C%2041.88%2C%2026.52%5D).%20Define%20the%20ankle%20joint%20center%20as%20the%20centroid%20of%20the%20**lm**%20and%20**mm**%20markers%2C%20and%20the%20knee%20joint%20center%20as%20the%20centroid%20of%20the%20**fh**%20and%20**mc**%20markers.%20An%20anatomical%20coordinate%20system%20for%20the%20leg%20can%20be%20defined%20as%20follows%3A%20the%20quasi-vertical%20axis%20(%24y%24)%20passes%20through%20the%20ankle%20and%20knee%20joint%20centers%3B%20a%20temporary%20medio-lateral%20axis%20(%24z%24)%20passes%20through%20the%20two%20markers%20on%20the%20malleoli%3B%20the%20anterior-posterior%20axis%20is%20the%20cross%20product%20of%20the%20two%20former%20axes%3B%20and%20the%20origin%20is%20at%20the%20ankle%20joint%20center.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20a)%20Calculate%20the%20anatomical%20coordinate%20system%20for%20the%20leg%20as%20described%20above.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20b)%20Calculate%20the%20rotation%20matrix%20and%20the%20translation%20vector%20for%20the%20transformation%20from%20the%20anatomical%20to%20the%20laboratory%20coordinate%20system.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20c)%20Calculate%20the%20position%20of%20each%20marker%20and%20of%20each%20joint%20center%20in%20the%20anatomical%20coordinate%20system.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20d)%20Calculate%20the%20Cardan%20angles%20using%20the%20%24zxy%24%20sequence%20for%20the%20orientation%20of%20the%20leg%20with%20respect%20to%20the%20laboratory%20(but%20remember%20that%20the%20letters%20chosen%20to%20refer%20to%20axes%20are%20arbitrary%3B%20what%20matters%20is%20the%20directions%20they%20represent).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20We%20solve%20parts%20a)%20to%20c)%20here.%20Part%20d)%20is%20Problem%203.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(np)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20calculation%20of%20the%20joint%20centers%0A%20%20%20%20mm%20%3D%20np.array(%5B2.71%2C%2010.22%2C%2026.52%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20lm%20%3D%20np.array(%5B2.92%2C%2010.10%2C%2018.85%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20fh%20%3D%20np.array(%5B5.05%2C%2041.90%2C%2015.41%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20mc%20%3D%20np.array(%5B8.29%2C%2041.88%2C%2026.52%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20ajc%20%3D%20(mm%20%2B%20lm)%20%2F%202%0A%20%20%20%20kjc%20%3D%20(fh%20%2B%20mc)%20%2F%202%0A%0A%20%20%20%20print(%22Position%20of%20the%20ankle%20joint%20center%3A%22%2C%20ajc)%0A%20%20%20%20print(%22Position%20of%20the%20knee%20joint%20center%3A%22%2C%20kjc)%0A%20%20%20%20return%20ajc%2C%20fh%2C%20kjc%2C%20lm%2C%20mc%2C%20mm%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(ajc%2C%20kjc%2C%20lm%2C%20mm%2C%20np)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20calculation%20of%20the%20anatomical%20coordinate%20system%20axes%20(basis)%0A%20%20%20%20y%20%3D%20kjc%20-%20ajc%0A%20%20%20%20x%20%3D%20np.cross(y%2C%20mm%20-%20lm)%0A%20%20%20%20z%20%3D%20np.cross(x%2C%20y)%0A%20%20%20%20print(%22Versors%3A%22)%0A%20%20%20%20x%20%3D%20x%20%2F%20np.linalg.norm(x)%0A%20%2 hen%20the%20columns%20have%20no%20names.%20The%20names%20of%20the%20markers%20are%20in%20the%20fourth%20line%20of%20the%20file%20and%20the%20coordinates%20in%20the%20fifth%2C%20so%20it%20is%20easier%20to%20read%20the%20header%20first%20and%20the%20numbers%20second.%20The%20function%20%60read_trc%60%2C%20from%20the%20%60functions%60%20folder%2C%20does%20that%2C%20and%20returns%20the%20header%20and%20a%20pandas%20DataFrame%20with%20one%20column%20per%20coordinate%20of%20each%20marker%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(read_trc)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_h%2C%20walk%20%3D%20read_trc(str(repo_file(%22data%2Fwalk.trc%22))%2C%20fname2%3D%22%22%2C%20dropna%3DFalse%2C%20na%3D0.0%2C%20fmt%3D%22uni%22)%0A%20%20%20%20walk.iloc%5B%3A5%2C%20%3A8%5D%0A%20%20%20%20return%20(walk%2C)%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20The%20right%20leg%20carries%20the%20same%20four%20markers%20as%20Winter's%20example%3A%20%60R.Ankle%60%20(lateral%20malleolus)%2C%20%60R.Ankle.Medial%60%2C%20%60R.HF%60%20(fibular%20head)%20and%20%60R.Knee.Medial%60.%20We%20convert%20them%20from%20millimetres%20to%20centimetres%20and%20apply%20Winter's%20definition%20to%20every%20frame%20at%20once%3B%20NumPy's%20cross%20product%20works%20row%20by%20row.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20One%20detail%20needs%20care.%20In%20Winter's%20data%20the%20medial%20malleolus%20has%20the%20larger%20%24z%24%20coordinate%2C%20so%20%24%5Cmathbf%7Bmm%7D%20-%20%5Cmathbf%7Blm%7D%24%20points%20along%20%24%2Bz%24%2C%20and%20%24%5Cmathbf%7By%7D%20%5Ctimes%20(%5Cmathbf%7Bmm%7D%20-%20%5Cmathbf%7Blm%7D)%24%20points%20forward.%20In%20our%20laboratory%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7D%24%20points%20to%20the%20right%2C%20so%20for%20the%20right%20leg%20it%20is%20the%20*lateral*%20malleolus%20that%20has%20the%20larger%20%24z%24%2C%20and%20we%20must%20use%20%24%5Cmathbf%7Blm%7D%20-%20%5Cmathbf%7Bmm%7D%24%20to%20keep%20the%20%24x%24%20axis%20pointing%20forward.%20It%20is%20the% %24%20around%20heel%20strike%2C%20with%20the%20ankle%20ahead%20of%20the%20knee%2C%20after%20which%20the%20shank%20rotates%20forward%20over%20the%20foot%20during%20stance.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%5Cbeta%24%2C%20the%20rotation%20about%20the%20long%20axis%2C%20stays%20between%20about%20%24-32%5Eo%24%20and%20%24-19%5Eo%24%3A%20the%20shank's%20coordinate%20system%20is%20rotated%20externally%2C%20with%20its%20%24x%24%20axis%20pointing%20forward%20and%20to%20the%20right.%20Part%20of%20the%20reason%20is%20anatomical%3A%20the%20line%20through%20the%20two%20malleoli%20is%20normally%20turned%20outwards%20relative%20to%20the%20axis%20of%20the%20knee%20(external%20tibial%20torsion)%2C%20and%20the%20definition%20we%20used%20takes%20its%20medio-lateral%20direction%20from%20the%20malleoli.%20Part%20is%20the%20posture%20of%20the%20whole%20leg%3A%20these%20angles%20are%20measured%20relative%20to%20the%20laboratory%2C%20so%20any%20outward%20turn%20of%20the%20leg%20relative%20to%20the%20direction%20of%20walking%20adds%20to%20them.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20And%20%24%5Calpha%24%20swings%20by%20about%2045%C2%B0%2C%20from%20%24-27%5Eo%24%20to%20%24%2B18%5Eo%24.%20Is%20the%20shank%20really%20tilting%20sideways%20that%20much%20at%20every%20stride%3F%20It%20is%20not.%20With%20a%20large%20sagittal%20rotation%20applied%20*last*%20and%20a%20coordinate%20system%20turned%20about%20its%20long%20axis%2C%20the%20%24xyz%24%20decomposition%20attributes%20part%20of%20the%20sagittal%20motion%20to%20%24%5Calpha%24%3A%20the%20same%20orientations%2C%20described%20in%20another%20order%2C%20would%20give%20a%20much%20smaller%20frontal%20angle.%20This%20%22cross-talk%22%20between%20angles%20is%20another%20face%20of%20the%20dependence%20on%20the%20sequence%2C%20and%20one%20reason%20why%20the%20flexion%E2%80%93extension%20axis%20is%20placed%20first%20in%20biomechanics.%20Problem%208%20asks%20you%20to%20check%20it.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Finally%2C%20the%20distance%20between%20the%20two%20joint%20centers%2C%20which%20should%20be%20constant%20for%20a%20rigid%20leg%2C%20varies%20by%20about%201.3%20cm%20during%20the%20trial.%20The%20markers%20move%20on%20the%20skin%2C%20and%20the%20leg%20is%20rigid%20only%20approximately%3B%20see%20%5BDetermination%20of%20a%20coordinate%20system%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fcoordinate_system.py)%20for%20what%20that%20does%20to%20the%20axes.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Challenge%202.**%20Add%20a%20horizontal%20line%20at%20the%20angles%20of%20the%20leg%20in%20Winter's%20static%20example%20(calculated%20with%20%60euler_angles_from_rot_xyz(RlG)%60)%20to%20the%20figure.%20Is%20Winter's%20posture%20close%20to%20any%20instant%20of%20this%20stride%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20A%20marker%20hidden%20from%20the%20cameras%0A%0A%20%20%20%20In%20walking%2C%20the%20medial%20malleolus%20marker%20is%20often%20hidden%20from%20the%20cameras%20for%20a%20few%20frames%2C%20when%20the%20other%20leg%20passes%20in%20front%20of%20it.%20The%20transformation%20matrix%20is%20the%20standard%20way%20to%20fill%20such%20a%20gap.%20Three%20other%20markers%20on%20the%20same%20segment%2C%20visible%20throughout%2C%20define%20a%20technical%20coordinate%20system%20at%20every%20frame.%20In%20the%20last%20frame%20before%20the%20gap%2C%20we%20express%20the%20hidden%20marker%20in%20that%20coordinate%20system%2C%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BP_l%7D%20%3D%20%5Cmathbf%7BT_%7BGl%7D%5E%7B-1%7D%7D%5C%2C%5Cmathbf%7BP_G%7D%24%2C%20once.%20If%20the%20segment%20is%20rigid%2C%20those%20local%20coordinates%20do%20not%20change%2C%20so%20during%20the%20gap%20the%20marker%20is%20wherever%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BP_G%7D%20%3D%20%5Cmathbf%7BT_%7BGl%7D%7D%5C%2C%5Cmathbf%7BP_l%7D%24%20puts%20it%2C%20frame%20by%20frame.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Our%20trial%20has%20no%20gap%2C%20which%20is%20convenient%3A%20we%20can%20pretend%20that%20%60R.Ankle.Medial%60%20disappears%20for%200.2%20s%20of%20the%20swing%20phase%2C%20fill%20the%20gap%20from%20%60R.HF%60%2C%20%60R.TT%60%20(on%20the%20tibial%20tuberosity)%20and%20%60R.Ankle%60%2C%20and%20compare%20the%20result%20with%20the%20marker%20that%20was%20actually%20measured.%20The%20technical%20coordinate%20system%20is%20built%20with%20the%20recipe%20of%20the%20basis%20method%2C%20with%20its%20origin%20at%20the%20centroid%20of%20the%20three%20markers%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.function%0Adef%20transformation_from_markers(m1%2C%20m2%2C%20m3)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22Transformation%20matrices%20T_Gl%20of%20the%20technical%20coordinate%20system%20of%20three%20markers.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Each%20marker%20is%20an%20array%20of%20positions%2C%20one%20frame%20per%20row.%20The%20first%20axis%20is%0A%20%20%20%20along%20m2%20-%20m1%2C%20the%20second%20is%20perpendicular%20to%20the%20plane%20of%20the%20markers%2C%20the%0A%20%20%20%20third%20completes%20a%20right-handed%20basis%2C%20and%20the%20origin%20is%20the%20centroid%20of%20the%0A%20%20%20%20markers.%20Returns%20one%204x4%20matrix%20per%20frame.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20import%20numpy%20as%20np%0A%0A%20%20%20%20v1%20%3D%20m2%20-%20m1%0A%20%20%20%20v2%20%3D%20np.cross(v1%2C%20m3%20-%20m1)%0A%20%20%20%20v3%20%3D%20np.cross(v1%2C%20v2)%0A%20%20%20%20T%20%3D%20np.zeros((len(m1)%2C%204%2C%204))%0A%20%20%20%20T%5B%3A%2C%20%3A3%2C%20%3A3%5D%20%3D%20np.stack(%5Bv%20%2F%20np.linalg.norm(v%2C%20axis%3D1%2C%20keepdims%3DTrue)%20for%20v%20in%20(v1%2C%20v2%2C%20v3)%5D%2C%20axis%3D2)%0A%20%20%20%20T%5B%3A%2C%20%3A3%2C%203%5D%20%3D%20(m1%20%2B%20m2%20%2B%20m3)%20%2F%203%0A%20%20%20%20T%5B%3A%2C%203%2C%203%5D%20%3D%201%0A%20%20%20%20return%20T%0A%0A%0A%40app.function%0Adef%20fill_gap(hidden%2C%20m1%2C%20m2%2C%20m3%2C%20gap%2C%20ref)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22Positions%20of%20the%20marker%20%60hidden%60%20in%20the%20frames%20%60gap%60%2C%20from%20three%20markers%20of%20the%20same%20segment.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20local%20co inate%20system%20in%20any%20order.%20%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%2B%20%22With%20real%20markers%20they%20do%20not%2C%20because%20the%20first%20axis%20is%20taken%20exactly%20along%20the%20first%20pair%2C%20%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%2B%20%22and%20the%20same%20error%20of%20a%20few%20millimetres%20tilts%20a%20vector%208%20cm%20long%20four%20to%20five%20times%20more%20than%20a%20vector%2036%20cm%20long.%20%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%2B%20f%22The%20hidden%20marker%20is%20%7B_lever%3A.0f%7D%20cm%20from%20the%20origin%20of%20the%20technical%20coordinate%20system%2C%20%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%2B%20f%22so%20every%20tenth%20of%20a%20degree%20of%20error%20in%20the%20axes%20moves%20it%20by%20%7B10%20*%20_lever%20*%20np.radians(0.1)%3A.1f%7D%20mm.%20%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%2B%20%22In%20the%20first%20half%20of%20the%20gap%20the%20two%20curves%20agree%3A%20that%20part%20of%20the%20error%20comes%20from%20the%20skin%2C%20and%20no%20choice%20of%20axes%20removes%20it.%20%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%2B%20%22The%20late%20climb%20came%20from%20the%20short%20first%20axis.%20%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%2B%20%22The%20rule%20from%20%5BDetermination%20of%20a%20coordinate%20system%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fcoordinate_system.py)%20%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%2B%20%22applies%3A%20build%20the%20first%20axis%20from%20the%20two%20markers%20that%20are%20farthest%20apart.%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%5D%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20)%0 %20For%20the%20first%20two%20cases%2C%20deduce%20the%20rotation%20matrices%20from%20the%20Global%20to%20the%20local%20coordinate%20system%2C%20and%20for%20the%20other%20two%2C%20the%20rotation%20matrices%20from%20the%20local%20to%20the%20Global%20coordinate%20system.%0A%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Consider%20the%20data%20from%20problem%205%20in%20the%20notebook%20%5BFrame%20of%20reference%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Freference_frame.py)%2C%20where%20the%20following%20anatomical%20landmark%20positions%20are%20given%20(units%20in%20meters)%3A%20RASIS%3D%5B0.5%2C%200.8%2C%200.4%5D%2C%20LASIS%3D%5B0.55%2C%200.78%2C%200.1%5D%2C%20RPSIS%3D%5B0.3%2C%200.85%2C%200.2%5D%2C%20and%20LPSIS%3D%5B0.29%2C%200.78%2C%200.3%5D.%20Deduce%20the%20rotation%20matrices%20for%20the%20Global%20to%20anatomical%20coordinate%20system%20and%20for%20the%20anatomical%20to%20Global%20coordinate%20system.%0A%0A%20%20%20%203.%20For%20the%20data%20from%20the%20example%20with%20actual%20motion%20analysis%20data%2C%20calculate%20the%20Cardan%20angles%20using%20the%20%24zxy%24%20sequence%20for%20the%20orientation%20of%20the%20leg%20with%20respect%20to%20the%20laboratory%20(but%20remember%20that%20the%20letters%20chosen%20to%20refer%20to%20axes%20are%20arbitrary%3B%20what%20matters%20is%20the%20directions%20they%20represent).%0A%0A%20%20%20%204.%20Write%20down%20the%204%C3%974%20matrices%20for%20each%20of%20the%20following%20(adapted%20from%20a%20%5Bcomputer%20graphics%20exercise%20sheet%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fweb.archive.org%2Fweb%2F20200224231232%2Fhttp%3A%2F%2Fwww.eecs.qmul.ac.uk%2F~sgg%2Fcg%2FExers%2Ftransformations_ex.html)%20of%20Queen%20Mary%20University%20of%20London)%3A%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20a.%20To%20translate%20by%20the%20vector%20(1%2C%202%2C%203).%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20b.%20To%20scale%20with%20respect%20to%20the%20origin%20by%20the%20amount%20(2%2C%204%2C%206).%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20c.%20To%20rotate%20around%20the%20z%20axis%20by%2045%20degrees%20(note%20that%20sin%2045%C2%B0%20%3D%20cos%2045%C2%B0%20%3D%201%2F%E2%88%9A2).%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20d.%20To%20rotate%20around%20the%20x%20axis%20by%2045%20degrees.%0A%0A%20%20%20%205.%20Compute%20the%20variation%20of%20Codman's%20movement%20from%20Guiding%20question%200.2%3A%20starting%20from%20the%20arm%20hanging%20at%20the%20side%2C%20abduct%20the%20arm%2090%C2%B0%20in%20the%20frontal%20plane%2C%20then%20swing%20it%20horizontally%2090%C2%B0%20to%20the%20front%2C%20then%20lower%20it%2090%C2%B0%20in%20front%20of%20the%20body%20to%20the%20side.%20Write%20each%20movement%20as%20a%20rotation%20about%20a%20fixed%20axis%2C%20with%20its%20sign%2C%20and%20find%20where%20the%20palm%20faces%20at%20the%20end.%20What%20single%20rotation%20is%20equivalent%20to%20the%20whole%20sequence%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%206.%20For%20the%20%24zxz%24%20sequence%2C%20repeat%20the%20analysis%20of%20the%20section%20%22How%20close%20is%20too%20close%3F%22%3A%20find%20the%20value%20of%20%24%5Cbeta%24%20at%20which%20the%20sequence%20locks%2C%20write%20a%20function%20that%20computes%20the%20three%20%24zxz%24%20angles%20from%20a%20rotation%20matrix%2C%20and%20show%20how%20the%20errors%20in%20the%20angles%20grow%20near%20the%20lock.%0A%0A%20%20%20%207.%20The%20coordinate%20system%20of%20the%20thigh%20is%20rotated%20from%20the%20laboratory%20by%20the%20%24xyz%24%20Euler%20angles%20(5%C2%B0%2C%2010%C2%B0%2C%2030%C2%B0)%2C%20and%20that%20of%20the%20shank%20by%20(5%C2%B0%2C%2015%C2%B0%2C%20%E2%88%9220%C2%B0).%20Calculate%20the%20rotation%20matrix%20of%20the%20shank%20relative%20to%20the%20thigh%20and%20its%20%24xyz%24%20Euler%20angles.%20Are%20they%20the%20differences%20between%20the%20angles%20of%20the%20two%20segments%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%208.%20Repeat%20the%20analysis%20of%20the%20whole%20stride%20with%20the%20%24zxy%24%20sequence%2C%20which%20puts%20the%20rotation%20about%20the%20medio-lateral%20axis%20first.%20Use%20%60euler_rotmat%60%20to%20obtain%20the%20algebraic%20matrix%2C%20derive%20the%20formulas%20for%20the%20three%20angles%2C%20and%20plot%20them.%20Compare%20the%20frontal-plane%20angle%20with%20%24%5Calpha%24%20of%20the%20%24xyz%24%20sequence%2C%20and%20explain%20the%20difference.%0A%0A%20%20%20%209.%20Euler's%20rotation%20theorem%20also%20works%20the%20other%20way%20round%3A%20a%20rotation%20by%20the%20angle%20%24%5Ctheta%24%20about%20the%20axis%20%24%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bn%7D%7D%24%20has%20the%20rotation%20matrix%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BR%7D%20%3D%20%5Cmathbf%7BI%7D%20%2B%20%5Csin%5Ctheta%5C%2C%5Cmathbf%7BK%7D%20%2B%20(1%20-%20%5Ccos%5Ctheta)%5C%2C%5Cmathbf%7BK%7D%5E2%24%20(Rodrigues'%20formula)%2C%20where%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BK%7D%24%20is%20the%20matrix%20for%20which%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BK%7D%5Cmathbf%7Bv%7D%20%3D%20%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bn%7D%7D%20%5Ctimes%20%5Cmathbf%7Bv%7D%24%20for%20any%20vector%20%24%5Cmathbf%7Bv%7D%24.%20Write%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BK%7D%24%2C%20implement%20the%20formula%20as%20a%20function%2C%20and%20check%20it%20against%20%60axis_angle%60%20with%20the%20rotation%20of%20%2430%5Eo%24%2C%20%2445%5Eo%24%20and%20%2460%5Eo%24%20about%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BX%7D%24%2C%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BY%7D%24%20and%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BZ%7D%24%20from%20the%20section%20%22One%20rotation%20is%20enough%22.%0A%0A%20%20%20%2010.%20Expand%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BR_X%7D(%5Ctheta)%24%20and%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BR_Z%7D(%5Ctheta)%24%20to%20second%20order%20in%20%24%5Ctheta%24%20(%24%5Ccos%5Ctheta%20%5Capprox%201%20-%20%5Ctheta%5E2%2F2%24%2C%20%24%5Csin%5Ctheta%20%5Capprox%20%5Ctheta%24)%20and%20show%20that%20the%20two%20orders%20of%20the%20rotations%20differ%20by%20a%20rotation%20of%20approximately%20%24%5Ctheta%5E2%24%20radians%20about%20the%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BY%7D%24%20axis%2C%20as%20the%20table%20in%20%22How%20much%20does%20the%20order%20matter%3F%22%20suggests.%20Why%20does%20the%20axis%20of%20the%20difference%20tilt%20away%20from%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BY%7D%24%20for%20larger%20angles%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%2011.%20Using%20the%20four%20pelvic%20markers%20of%20%60walk.trc%60%20(%60R.ASIS%60%2C%20%60L.ASIS%60%2C%20%60R.PSIS%60%20and%20%60L.PSIS%60)%20and%20the%20VAKHUM%20convention%20of%20Problem%202%2C%20calculate%20the%20anatomical%20coordinate%20system%20of%20the%20pelvis%20at%20every%20frame%20of%20the%20stride%2C%20and%20plot%20its%20%24xyz%24%20Cardan%20angles%20relative%20to%20the%20laboratory.%20Which%20angle%20varies%20most%2C%20and%20by%20how%20much%3F%20Is%20the%20pelvis%20close%20to%20gimbal%20lock%20at%20any%20moment%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%2012.%20The%20right%20thigh%20in%20%60walk.trc%60%20carries%20the%20markers%20%60R.GTR%60%20(greater%20trochanter)%2C%20%60R.Knee%60%20(lateral%20epicondyle)%20and%20%60R.Knee.Medial%60.%20Define%20a%20coordinate%20system%20for%20the%20thigh%20in%20the%20same%20way%20as%20for%20the%20shank%20in%20the%20section%20%22A%20whole%20stride%22%20(the%20%24y%24%20axis%20from%20the%20knee%20joint%20center%2C%20midway%20between%20the%20two%20knee%20markers%2C%20to%20the%20greater%20trochanter%2C%20and%20a%20temporary%20medio-lateral%20axis%20from%20%60R.Knee.Medial%60%20to%20%60R.Knee%60).%20Calculate%20the%20rotation%20matrix%20of%20the%20shank%20relative%20to%20the%20thigh%20at%20every%20frame%2C%20and%20use%20%60axis_angle%60%20to%20plot%20the%20total%20rotation%20of%20the%20knee%20during%20the%20stride.%20When%20is%20it%20largest%3F%20Why%20is%20it%20not%20zero%20when%20the%20knee%20is%20at%20its%20straightest%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%20details%20%7C%20Final%20answers%20to%20the%20problems%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20For%20positive%2090%C2%B0%20turns%20and%20the%20figure%E2%80%99s%20four%20rows%3A%20fixed%20X%20then%20Y%2C%20global-to-local%20%24%5B%5B0%2C0%2C-1%5D%2C%5B1%2C0%2C0%5D%2C%5B0%2C-1%2C0%5D%5D%24%3B%20fixed%20Y%20then%20X%2C%20global-to-local%20%24%5B%5B0%2C1%2C0%5D%2C%5B0%2C0%2C1%5D%2C%5B1%2C0%2C0%5D%5D%24%3B%20local%20x%20then%20y%2C%20local-to-global%20%24%5B%5B0%2C0%2C1%5D%2C%5B1%2C0%2C0%5D%2C%5B0%2C1%2C0%5D%5D%24%3B%20local%20y%20then%20x%2C%20local-to-global%20%24%5B%5B0%2C1%2C0%5D%2C%5B0%2C0%2C-1%5D%2C%5B-1%2C0%2C0%5D%5D%24.%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Global-to-pelvis%20%24R%3D%5B%5B0.980530%2C-0.098327%2C0.169977%5D%2C%5B0.107934%2C0.992988%2C-0.048210%5D%2C%5B-0.164045%2C0.065618%2C0.984268%5D%5D%24.%20Pelvis-to-global%20is%20%24R%5ET%24.%0A%20%20%20%203.%20Intrinsic%20%24zxy%24%20angles%20for%20the%20static%20leg%20example%20are%20approximately%20%24(-6.92713%2C-3.08021%2C-1.66623)%5E%5Ccirc%24.%0A%20%20%20%204.%20(a)%20%24%5B%5B1%2C0%2C0%2C1%5D%2C%5B0%2C1%2C0%2C2%5D%2C%5B0%2C0%2C1%2C3%5D%2C%5B0%2C0%2C0%2C1%5D%5D%24.%20(b)%20%24%5Coperatorname%7Bdiag%7D(2%2C4%2C6%2C1)%24.%20With%20%24q%3D1%2F%5Csqrt2%24%3A%20(c)%20%24%5B%5Bq%2C-q%2C0%2C0%5D%2C%5Bq%2Cq%2C0%2C0%5D%2C%5B0%2C0%2C1%2C0%5D%2C%5B0%2C0%2C0%2C1%5D%5D%24%3B%20(d)%20%24%5B%5B1%2C0%2C0%2C0%5D%2C%5B0%2Cq%2C-q%2C0%5D%2C%5B0%2Cq%2Cq%2C0%5D%2C%5B0%2C0%2C0%2C1%5D%5D%24.%0A%20%20%20%205.%20With%20%24X%24%20anterior%2C%20%24Y%24%20upward%20and%20%24Z%24%20right%3A%20%24R_Z(-90%5E%5Ccirc)R_Y(90%5E%5Ccirc)R_X(-90%5E%5Ccirc)%3DR_Y(90%5E%5Ccirc)%24.%20The%20right%20palm%20ends%20facing%20backward%2C%20opposite%20to%20the%20original%20sequence%E2%80%99s%20result.%0A%20%20%20%206.%20%24zxz%24%20locks%20at%20middle%20angle%20%24%5Cbeta%3D0%24%20or%20%24%5Cpi%24.%20For%20local-to-global%20matrix%20%24A%24%20away%20from%20the%20lock%2C%20%24%5Cbeta%3D%5Carccos%20A_%7B22%7D%24%2C%20%24%5Calpha%3D%5Coperatorname%7Batan2%7D(A_%7B02%7D%2C-A_%7B12%7D)%24%2C%20%24%5Cgamma%3D%5Coperatorname%7Batan2%7D(A_%7B20%7D%2CA_%7B21%7D)%24.%20Angle-error%20amplification%20scales%20with%20%241%2F%7C%5Csin%5Cbeta%7C%24%3B%20at%20the%20lock%20the%20individual%20outer%20angles%20are%20not%20unique.%0A%20%20%20%207.%20Shank-to-thigh%20rotation%20is%20approximately%20%24%5B%5B0.639691%2C0.764917%2C0.075479%5D%2C%5B-0.764257%2C0.643438%2C-0.043578%5D%2C%5B-0.081900%2C-0.029809%2C0.996195%5D%5D%24.%20Intrinsic%20xyz%20angles%20are%20%24(2.50477%2C4.32875%2C-50.09468)%5E%5Ccirc%24%3B%20they%20are%20not%20the%20componentwise%20differences.%0A%20%20%20%208.%20For%20local-to-global%20%24A%24%2C%20%24%5Cbeta%3D%5Carcsin%20A_%7B21%7D%24%2C%20%24%5Calpha%3D%5Coperatorname%7Batan2%7D(-A_%7B01%7D%2CA_%7B11%7D)%24%2C%20%24%5Cgamma%3D%5Coperatorname%7Batan2%7D(-A_%7B20%7D%2CA_%7B22%7D)%24.%20The%20stride%20ranges%20in%20z%2Cx%2Cy%20order%20are%20approximately%20%5B%E2%88%9258.545%2C29.879%5D%C2%B0%2C%20%5B%E2%88%921.855%2C6.236%5D%C2%B0%2C%20%5B%E2%88%9235.699%2C%E2%88%9220.707%5D%C2%B0.%20The%20frontal%20excursion%20is%20much%20smaller%20than%20in%20xyz%20because%20the%20decomposition%20assigns%20rotations%20differently.%0A%20%20%20%209.%20%24K%3D%5B%5B0%2C-n_z%2Cn_y%5D%2C%5Bn_z%2C0%2C-n_x%5D%2C%5B-n_y%2Cn_x%2C0%5D%5D%24%3B%20%60I%20%2B%20sin(theta)*K%20%2B%20(1-cos(theta))*(K%40K)%60%20reproduces%20the%20same%20axis-angle%20rotation%20to%20numerical%20precision.%0A%20%20%20%2010.%20The%20leading%20order%20difference%20is%20a%20rotation%20of%20magnitude%20%24%5Ctheta%5E2%24%20about%20Y%2C%20with%20sign%20determined%20by%20the%20order%20used%20for%20comparison.%20Higher-order%20commutator%20terms%20add%20X%20and%20Z%20components%20at%20finite%20angles%2C%20tilting%20the%20equivalent%20axis.%0A%20%20%20%2011.%20Pelvis%20xyz%20ranges%20are%20about%20%5B%E2%88%928.887%2C3.463%5D%C2%B0%2C%20%5B%E2%88%925.608%2C9.246%5D%C2%B0%2C%20%5B%E2%88%924.781%2C1.701%5D%C2%B0.%20The%20Y%20angle%20varies%20most%2C%20by%2014.854%C2%B0%3B%20its%20distance%20from%20%C2%B190%C2%B0%20confirms%20that%20this%20recording%20is%20far%20from%20the%20xyz%20lock.%0A%20%20%20%2012.%20Total%20relative%20rotation%20ranges%20approximately%2019.569%E2%80%9369.987%C2%B0%2C%20largest%20at%20zero-based%20frame%2019%2C%20time%200.127%20s.%20Its%20nonzero%20minimum%20reflects%20the%20anatomical%2Ftechnical%20axis%20definitions%2C%20three-dimensional%20rotation%20and%20marker%2Fsoft-tissue%20effects%3B%20it%20is%20not%20a%20pure%20c
